stem: Pneumothorax is potentially life-threatening if it is a tension pneumothorax. Which one of the following is NOT a sign of tension pneumothorax?
explanation: Hypoglycaemia is not a sign of tension pneumothorax. Typical signs include hypoxia, tachycardia, hypotension, distended neck veins, and tracheal deviation.

citations.title: Practice Quiz: Emergency medicine - Trauma 1 - Primary survey

rationale: The question asks for the option that is not a sign of tension pneumothorax. Hypoglycaemia is unrelated, whereas the other options are recognised signs or consequences of tension pneumothorax.

optionExplanations.A: Can occur due to impaired ventilation and oxygenation.
optionExplanations.B: A common compensatory response to shock and hypoxia.
optionExplanations.C: Occurs with obstructive shock from a tension pneumothorax.
optionExplanations.D: May be seen due to raised intrathoracic pressure.
optionExplanations.E: Not a feature of tension pneumothorax.
optionExplanations.F: A classic late sign of tension pneumothorax.

source.questionTextHtml: Pneumothorax is potentially life-threatening if it is a tension pneumothorax. In this case, you need to consider other signs. Which one of the following is NOT a sign you need to consider for tension pneumothorax?

Clinical scenario 1 - James

Teaching/learning points:

Initial ABC approach to trauma patient

Recognition of life-threatening injury and resuscitation priorities

You receive a pre-hospital alert from paramedics regarding James, a four year-old boy who ran away from his mother onto the road, where he was hit by a van at approximately 50kph. He hit the windscreen and was thrown approximately 7 metres. He was unconscious at the scene and not moving spontaneously. The paramedic crew on the scene report him to be unconscious but breathing, with a respiratory rate of 30/min, heart rate 120bpm, multiple abrasions and bruises. ETA 10 minutes.

The following 12 questions refer to James' clinical scenario.
